==English==
{{examples|{{listen|Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky - romeo and juliet- overture-fantasy.ogg|a piece of '''music''' ({{w|Tchaikovsky}}'s ''Romeo and Juliet Overture'', performed by the Skidmore College Orchestra)}}}}
{{wp}}
{{wikiquote}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|musick|musicke|musique|musike}} (obsolete)

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*men- (think)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|musik}}, {{m|enm|musike}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|musik}}, {{m|fro|musike}}, {{der|en|fro|musique}}, and their source {{der|en|la|mūsica}}, from {{der|en|grc|μουσική}}, from {{der|en|grc|Μοῦσα||Muse}}, an Ancient Greek deity of the arts. {{surf|en|muse|-ic|t2=pertaining to}}. In this sense, displaced native {{cog|ang|drēam||music}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|dream}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|myo͞oʹzĭk|a=RP}} {{IPA|en|/ˈmjuːzɪk/}}
* {{audio|en|En-uk-music.ogg|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈmjuzɪk/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-music.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{hyphenation|en|mus|ic}}
* {{rhymes|en|uːzɪk|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|-|s}}

# A [[series]] of [[sound#Noun|sounds]] [[organize]]d in [[time#Noun|time]], usually [[employ#Verb|employing]] some [[combination]] of [[harmony]], [[melody]], [[rhythm]], [[tempo]], etc., often to [[convey]] a [[mood]].
#: {{ux|en|I keep listening to this '''music''' because it’s a masterpiece.}}
#* {{RQ:Congreve Mourning Bride|page=1|passage='''Muſick''' has Charms to ſooth a ſavage Breaſt, / To ſoften Rocks, or bend a knotted Oak.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-11-22|author=Ian Sample|volume=189|issue=24|page=32|magazine=The Guardian Weekly|title=Music lessons in early childhood may improve brain's performance|url=http://www.theguardian.com/science/2013/nov/12/music-lessons-early-childhood-brain-performance|passage='''Music''' lessons in early childhood lead to changes in the brain that could improve its performance far into adulthood, researchers say.}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively}} Any [[interesting#Adjective|interesting]] or [[pleasing#Adjective|pleasing]] sounds.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1856|author=John Esten Cooke|title=The Virginia Comedians|url=http://www.worldcat.org/title/virginia-comedians-or-old-days-in-the-old-dominion-edited-from-the-mss-of-c-effingham-esq-or-rather-written-by-john-esten-cooke/oclc/559686172|page=247|text=“Oh! this was very kind,” she said, with that simplicity and tenderness, which at times made her voice pure '''music''', “I could not have expected you so soon.”}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=19 Aug 78|volume=6|number=5|journal=Gay Community News|page=15|author=Kevin Warren|title=A Flawless Production|text=Wilson's definite genius for rapid, witty dialogue which becomes a kind of conversational '''music''' at times.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q638}}An [[art form]], [[create]]d by organizing [[pitch#Noun|pitch]], rhythm, and sounds made using [[musical instrument]]s and/or [[singing#Noun|singing]].
# A [[guide#Noun|guide]] to [[play#Verb|playing]] or [[sing#Verb|singing]] a particular [[tune#Noun|tune]]; [[sheet music]].
# {{lb|en|military|slang}} [[electronic|Electronic]] [[signal#Noun|signal]] [[jamming#Noun|jamming]].
# {{lb|en|US|slang|dated}} [[heated#Adjective|Heated]] [[argument#Noun|argument]].
# {{lb|en|US|slang|dated}} [[fun|Fun]]; [[amusement]].

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[seduce]] or [[entice]] with music.

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# {{lb|en|rare}} [[musical|Musical]].<ref>{{R:OED Online|entry=music|pos=''n.'' and ''adj.''|noformat=1|id=7569208909}}</ref>
#* {{quote-book|en|author=[[w:Theophilus Gale|T[heophilus] G[ale]]]|title=The Court of the Gentiles: or A Discourse Touching the Original of Human Literature, Both Philologie and Philosophie, from the Scriptures, and Jewish Church in Order to a Demonstration,{{nb...|of 1. The Perfection of Gods VVord, and Church Light. 2: The Imperfection of Natures Light, and Mischief of Vain Philosophie. 3. The Right Use of Human Learning, and Especially Sound Philosophie.}}|volume_plain=part I (Of Philologie)|location=Oxon [Oxford]|publisher={{...|Printed by}} Hen[ry] Hall for Tho[mas] Gilbert|year=1669|pages=136–137|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/bim_early-english-books-1641-1700_the-court-of-the-gentile_gale-theophilus_1669/page/137/mode/1up|passage=Again, ''Moſes'' was the firſt that brought in ''ſacred Muſick'': thus in like manner ''Strabo lib''. 10. 453. informes us, that the ''Bacchick Muſick'' was famous throughout ''Aſia''; and that many '''''muſick''' Inſtruments'' had obteined a ''Barbarick name'', as ''Jambla'', ''Sambuke'', ''Barbitos'', ''Magades'', &c. which ſeem all to be of ''Hebrew origination''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Jones Very|chapter=The Unrevealed|editor=Helen R. Deese|title=Jones Very: The Complete Poems|location=Athens, Ga.|publisher=w:University of Georgia Press|start_month=fall|start_year=1838|month=summer|year=1839|year_published=1993|page=159|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/jonesverycomplet0000very/page/159/mode/1up|lines=4–9|isbn=0-8203-1481-1|passage=Loosened / Thy tongue shall with sweet-flowing sounds surprize / The ear of sense; another than thyself / Will be seen within to have come, and bringing / '''Music''' tones from other spheres to have made / Thee ever the harp of hidden minstrelsy.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=[[w:William Ellery Channing (poet)|William Ellery Channing]]|chapter=The Desert|title=Poems|volume_plain=second series|location=Boston, Mass.|publisher=James Munroe and Company|year=1847|page=59|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/poems00chan/page/59/mode/1up|passage=So should she drape the World’s wide round, / With sunny robes, and fresh Spring weather / And consecrate the loneliest ground, / While we went wandering linked together, / Her '''music''' voice, her beaming eyes, / Give to the Silence, glad replies.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=[[w:Sarah Josepha Hale|Sarah J[osepha] Hale]]|title=The Judge; a Drama of American Life|editor=Sarah J[osepha] Hale|journal=[[w:Godey's Lady's Book|Godey’s Lady’s Book]]|volume=XLII|location=Philadelphia, Pa.|publisher=[[w:Louis Antoine Godey|L[ouis] A[ntoine] Godey]]|month=January|year=1851|section=act I, scene III|page=26|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/GodeySMagazine1851/page/n46/mode/1up|column=2|passage=And therefore, prisoner, you are doomed for life / To solitary toil. Alone! alone! alone! / Love’s '''music''' voice will never greet your ear; / Affection’s eye will never meet your gaze; / Nor heart-warm hand of friend return your grasp; / But morn, and noon, and night, days, months, and years, / Will all be told in this one word—alone!}}
